call_points.text: Management declined to guide full-year EBITDA margin, saying it is too early to estimate.
New plants should contribute to the bottom line from Q3 and definitely Q4, lifting the base level by year-end.
Total spend on the two projects is around ₹3,850 Cr, within the approved capex envelope.
Net debt is around ₹4,700-4,800 Cr, near peak; deleveraging should start reflecting from this year.
Interest on project loans is being capitalised; the new plants will be depreciated over 25 years.
Equinor LNG supply began in May; old contracts phase out by Q4, after which Equinor covers the full requirement.
DMSL is committed in principle to a listing, but the route (demerger or IPO) is not yet decided.
Ammonia is around USD 600 FOB Middle East; management expects elevated levels for at least some more quarters.
Management said it is hearing Russia may consider an FGAN export ban from October this year.
Gopalpur TAN utilisation expected to reach 90-95% on a TPD basis by end of FY27, full utilisation the year after.
FY27 capex seen including maintenance; normal maintenance capex from next year.
Net debt ₹4,824 Cr with net debt/EBITDA ~2.86x; management declined to give an FY27 debt number.
call_points.versus_prior: FY27 net leverage target of 2-2.2x in memory; no new debt target given

call_points.text: Equinor LNG contract gives supply surety and cost benefit, but management would not quantify the gas cost saving.
TAN Q4 volume rose 12% YoY and 27% QoQ on year-end mining targets; Q2 is seasonally weaker but no long-term demand destruction seen.
IPA prices are elevated on LPG/RGP shortage; management expects them to stay high for some time before a lower new normal.
Receivables and inventory days rose on soft fertiliser demand and higher channel inventory; management calls it temporary and expects normalisation in a month or two.
No timeline for the DMSL subsidiary listing/demerger; management says form, shape and timing are yet to be decided.
Chardham Chemicals had no revenue last year; the plan is to revamp the facility to Deepak standards with no large capex expected.
call_points.versus_prior: acquisition completed 6 May 2026 at ₹121.45 Cr per memory

call_points.text: Management expects FY27 growth and margins to improve on global supply tightness, Equinor gas and new capacity, without giving numbers.

operating_notes.text: Mahadhan AgriTech Limited (MAL) is a wholly owned material subsidiary of Deepak Fertilisers.

Promoter group holding in Deepak Fertilisers was 45.63% (5,76,03,547 shares) both before and after the 22 April 2026 inter-se transfer of 74,00,000 shares from Robust Marketing Services to SCM Commercial.

Chardham Chemicals Private Limited (CCPL), incorporated 5 March 2021, New Delhi, was acquired 100% by Deepak Mining Solutions Limited for ₹121.45 Cr cash on 6 May 2026; turnover was Nil in FY2022-23, FY2023-24 and FY2024-25.
DMSL has a 100% owned mining servicing subsidiary in Australia, named in the filing as an export channel for CCPL's differentiated explosives products.
Received a tax and penalty demand of ₹74.89 Cr under MVAT for FY2026-27 from the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Pune.

TAN expansion at Gopalpur, Odisha adds 3,77,000 MTPA at a project cost of ~₹2,675 Cr, funded with ₹1,541 Cr debt; nitric acid expansion at Dahej, Gujarat (900 TPD weak nitric acid and 450 TPD concentrated nitric acid) costs ~₹1,983 Cr at a
Physical completion was over 93% for the TAN project and over 86% for the nitric acid project as on 31 March 2026.
DFPCL holds around 40% market share in TAN and is the largest domestic nitric acid maker and leading IPA maker; CRISIL expects interest coverage above 5x over the medium term.
FY26 TAN sales volume 577 KT (+11% YoY) at 98% capacity utilisation; Q4 volume 164 KT, up 12% YoY and 27% QoQ.
Q4FY26 capacity utilisation: DNA 104%, CNA 76%, IPA 81% (planned shutdown); IPA pricing weakness continued through FY26.
Crop Nutrition FY26 revenue ₹6,166 Cr (+20% YoY); Q4 ANP 75% and NPK 54% utilisation; IMD sees 2026 monsoon at 92% of LPA.
FY26 TAN volume growth ~11% YoY; Q4 volume up 12% YoY and 27% QoQ on year-end mining targets.
B2C ~16% of Mining Chemicals revenue (13% last year); Specialty and Croptek ~33% of Crop Nutrition revenue (30% last year).
Ammonia last published price ~$800 Middle East FOB; PCL produces 500,000+ tonnes of ammonia and also trades imported ammonia.
Ammonia plant ran at 94% utilisation in Q1FY27 and was debottlenecked, adding almost 10% capacity; about 80% of ammonia is captive consumption.
Gopalpur TAN about 96% complete and Dahej nitric acid about 93% complete, both expected to start in Q2FY27 with total spend of around ₹3,850 Cr.
Merchant nitric acid sales were flat YoY at around 80 KT in Q1FY27; ammonia was around USD 600 FOB Middle East on the call.
Gopalpur TAN project is ~95% physically complete with ₹2,251 Cr incurred out of ₹2,675 Cr outlay.

timeline.summary: On 21 April 2026, Deepak Fertilisers disclosed a ₹0.55 Cr GST demand and penalty order dated 25 March 2026 against its wholly owned subsidiary Mahadhan AgriTech over disallowed CENVAT credit, which MAL plans to appeal.

On 28 April 2026, SCM Commercial Private Limited reported acquiring 74,00,000 shares (5.86%) of Deepak Fertilisers from Robust Marketing Services in an off-market inter-se promoter transfer on 22 April 2026, leaving the promoter group at 45.63%.

On 6 May 2026, wholly owned subsidiary Deepak Mining Solutions completed the cash acquisition of 100% of explosives maker Chardham Chemicals Private Limited for ₹121.45 Cr, per the 24 December 2025 agreement; the target had nil turnover in each of the last three years.
On 12 May 2026, Deepak Fertilisers disclosed a ₹74.89 Cr tax demand and penalty order dated 31 March 2026 issued by the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Pune.

Deepak Fertilizers and Petrochemicals Corporation Limited’s **Kumar Purohit (VP – Legal, Compliance & Company Secretary)** scheduled an earnings conference call on **May 29, 2026, at 4:00 PM IST** to discuss Q4FY26 and FY26 results.

On 27 May 2026, CRISIL reaffirmed Deepak Fertilisers at Crisil AA-/Positive and Crisil A1+, cutting total rated bank facilities to ₹1,125 Cr from ₹3,000 Cr after withdrawing ₹1,875 Cr of facilities and ₹750 Cr of commercial paper at the company's request.
Deepak Fertilizers’ Board recommended a final dividend of ₹10 per equity share for FY2026, payable within 30 days of the AGM.

On 29 May 2026 Deepak Fertilisers' Q4FY26 call said Gopalpur TAN (~95% complete) and Dahej nitric acid (~86%) would commission in Q2FY27, a quarter later than earlier guided, with net debt at ₹4,824 Cr (2.86x EBITDA).

On its 31 July 2026 Q1FY27 call, Deepak Fertilisers said Gopalpur TAN (96% complete) and Dahej nitric acid (93%) would start in Q2FY27, with ₹3,850 Cr spent so far and net debt at ₹4,719 Cr (1.4x EBITDA).
ICRA reaffirmed Deepak Fertilisers' rating at [ICRA]AA-, removed it from watch, and assigned a Positive outlook.
